_help._file: The 3 AI skills: HOW WELL it plays (what it wants is the personality — personalities.json). Any personality can play at any skill. Starting values from design/ai.md's skills table; candidate counts get checked by the phone-speed timing spike (F38 task 1). Notes are keyed by the setting's name inside ONE skill.
_help.id: The skill's name in code. Its name for players lives in content/text/en.json → ai.skill.<id>.
_help.candidates: The most moves it looks at in one decision. More = finds better moves, thinks longer.
_help.worlds: How many versions of the hidden seeds (rivals' hands, the bag) it imagines and averages over. More = fewer surprises.
_help.spread: 0–1: it keeps moves within this share of its best one (1 = only the very best).
_help.topN: …and picks among at most this many of them, weighted by how good they are. Fewer = sharper.
_help.wobble: 0–1: widens every trait range around its centre — a less skilled player is less consistent.
_help.beliefNoise: 0–1: how blurry its guess of everyone's secret Magic is. Higher = misreads who's winning more often (and calls the game wrong more often).
_help.extras.zipf: Vocabulary: it only AIMS for words at least this common (Zipf score; 3 ≈ 22k words, 2 ≈ 44k, 0 = all 63k). The personality's vocabulary modifier is added. Any word it makes by accident still counts.

_labels.spread: Picks within this share of its best move (0–1)
_labels.extras.zipf: Vocabulary: aims only for words this common (Zipf)
